claims.text: Severe cryo-rolling followed by annealing can tailor heterogeneous microstructures in brittle intermetallic-containing high-entropy alloys.
Severe cryo-rolling followed by annealing can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
The investigated material is CoCrFeNi2.1Nb0.2 with an FCC matrix containing complex Laves-phase particles.
The ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
The alloy was multi-pass rolled to a 90% thickness reduction and a final thickness of approximately 0.4 mm.
Cryo-rolling involved immersion in liquid nitrogen for 0.5 h before and after every pass.
Rolling was followed by annealing at 800 °C for 1 h and water quenching.
The resulting heterogeneous microstructure contains co-existing deformed and recrystallized regions.
The higher density of dislocations, shear bands, and grain boundaries in the cryo-rolled alloy accelerates nanosized epsilon-phase precipitation early during recrystallization.
The nanosized epsilon-phase precipitates pin high-angle boundaries through Zener pinning.
Boundary pinning inhibits recrystallization and produces a mixture of deformed and recrystallized regions.
Mechanical incompatibility between deformed and recrystallized regions generates strain gradients and geometrically necessary dislocations.
The geometrically necessary dislocations produce long-range back stress.
Long-range back stress delays necking and enhances both strength and ductility.
The cryo-rolled and annealed alloy achieves a yield strength of 1219 ± 14 MPa.
The cryo-rolled and annealed alloy achieves an ultimate tensile strength of 1272 ± 25 MPa.
The cryo-rolled and annealed alloy achieves approximately 22% elongation.
The cold-rolled and annealed baseline has a yield strength of 774 ± 13 MPa, ultimate tensile strength of 1085 ± 18 MPa, and approximately 20% elongation.
The back stress generated by the heterogeneous microstructure was not quantified in the study.
The stability of the nanodomains during long-term storage and deformation is not fully understood.
